title: A trip to Almaty
paragraphs: My name is Madina Tolenova. I am twenty years old and I am from Shymkent, in the south of Kazakhstan. I study Tourism and Hospitality at WKU — it is my second year, and I love learning about travel, culture, and different places. Last month, my classmate Sabina and I visited Almaty — the biggest city in Kazakhstan — for the first time. We arrived on a Friday morning and had the whole weekend to explore. We were both incredibly excited.

We arrived at Almaty Station early in the morning. The station is in the north-east of the city, not far from the mountains. We stood in front of the main entrance for a moment and looked around. On the left side of the entrance, there was a large board with the train timetable. On the right side, there were rows of small shops and a busy café. A taxi driver was waiting next to our platform with a sign that had our names on it. We put our bags in the boot of his car and drove towards the city centre.

Our first stop was Panfilov Park — the most famous park in Almaty. It is in the heart of the city, between two wide avenues: Gogol Street and Kabar Avenue. In the centre of the park, there is a beautiful wooden cathedral — the Zenkov Cathedral. It stands between tall, ancient trees and is painted in bright colours: blue, yellow, and white. We walked slowly in front of it and took many photographs. There was a fountain at the bottom of the steps, and small children were playing around it. We sat on a bench opposite the cathedral and ate fresh apples that we had brought from the train.

After the park, we went to the Green Bazaar — one of the most famous markets in Central Asia. It is about five minutes on foot from Panfilov Park, just behind the central post office. We walked along Zhibek Zholy Street to get there. Inside, everything was colourful and noisy. On the left side of the entrance, sellers were offering fresh fruit — enormous apples, sweet pears, and huge watermelons. On the right side, there were rows of spices and herbs with incredible smells. Above the stalls, bright lamps and colourful banners made the whole place feel warm and alive. I bought a bag of dried apricots, some walnuts, and a small jar of mountain honey to take back to my friends at WKU.

On Saturday, we took a cable car up to Shymbulak — a famous mountain resort high in the Zailiysky Alatau mountains, about twenty-five kilometres from the city centre. The cable car started at Medeu, at the bottom of the valley, and carried us slowly up to the resort at the top. From above, the view of Almaty was breathtaking. The city looked small and orderly far below us, with the flat steppe stretching endlessly to the north and the high mountains rising to the south. We stood on the observation platform next to the main building and looked in every direction. The air at the top was cold, clean, and wonderfully fresh.

We returned to Uralsk on Sunday evening — tired, happy, and full of wonderful memories. Back in my dormitory room at WKU, I spread all my purchases out on my bed and thought about everything we had seen. For a Tourism student, Almaty was like a living textbook — every street, every park, every market had something to teach me. I am already planning my next trip. This time, I want to travel to Turkestan in the south of Kazakhstan to see the magnificent Khoja Ahmed Yasawi Mausoleum. There is always more to explore.

dialogue.speaker: Sabina
dialogue.text: Madina! Your photos from Almaty are absolutely amazing. Which place was your favourite?

dialogue.speaker: Madina
dialogue.text: The Green Bazaar, without a doubt. The colours, the smells — everything was incredible.

dialogue.speaker: Sabina
dialogue.text: Was the Zenkov Cathedral as beautiful as in the photos?

dialogue.speaker: Madina
dialogue.text: Even more beautiful! It stood between these huge old trees — totally breathtaking.

dialogue.speaker: Sabina
dialogue.text: Did you go up to Shymbulak? What was the view like from the top?

dialogue.speaker: Madina
dialogue.text: We stood on the platform next to the main building. The whole city was far below us!

dialogue.speaker: Sabina
dialogue.text: Was the Green Bazaar easy to find from Panfilov Park?

dialogue.speaker: Madina
dialogue.text: Very easy — just behind the post office, five minutes along the street.

dialogue.speaker: Sabina
dialogue.text: What did you buy at the bazaar?

dialogue.speaker: Madina
dialogue.text: Dried apricots, walnuts, and the most amazing jar of mountain honey!

dialogue.speaker: Sabina
dialogue.text: Where do you want to go next?

dialogue.speaker: Madina
dialogue.text: Turkestan! I want to see the Yasawi Mausoleum in the south of the country.
